info.name: Pesticides OCR Backend: External User RBAC
info.description:
Applicant self-service access to an EXISTING registration (view/edit), built on top of magic-link email verification. This collection covers only the RBAC-specific additions — for the underlying request/resend/verify flow itself, see `email-verification-magic-link.postman_collection.json`.

Full spec: `external-user-rbac-spec.html`. Design decisions (all confirmed): `magic-link-tickets.md` → "Complete secure applicant access to registrations: decisions confirmed".

## Setup
1. Set `baseUrl` (local default `http://localhost:3001`).
2. Set `journeyTokenSecret` to the backend's `JOURNEY_TOKEN_SECRET` (same as the email-verification collection).
3. Set `email` to an address on the Notify team-key guest list, OR skip real email sending by seeding a verification record directly in Mongo and setting `linkToken` yourself (the API never returns the raw token, by design) — see `scripts/test-external-user-flow.js` for how the automated test script does this.
4. Submit a registration first (folder 1) to get a `reference` and set it, with `contactEmail` matching `email`.

## Why two tokens look similar but aren't
`x-journey-token` binds a request to one frontend session (used throughout email verification). `externalAccessToken` (returned by verify, only when `reference` is supplied) is a completely different, longer-lived credential scoped to one registration. Don't confuse the two — they use different secrets and neither can substitute for the other.

exec: // Signs the journey token the same way the frontend/backend do: <nonce>.<hex HMAC-SHA256(nonce)>.
if (!secret) { throw new Error('Set the journeyTokenSecret collection variable to the backend JOURNEY_TOKEN_SECRET') }

item.name: 1. Set up test registrations
item.description: Create your own registration (contact email = {{email}}) and a second, unrelated one (different contact email), so entitlement checks have something real to pass and fail against.

request.description: Submitting bypasses the email-verification gate on /register in most local setups (EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED_FOR_REGISTRATION=false by default) — if your tier has it enabled, run the full email-verification collection's 'Happy path' folder first instead.

item.name: 2. Verify with reference (entitlement + token issuance)
item.description: Before each request here, make sure `linkToken` holds a fresh, unused link requested for `{{email}}` (see the email-verification collection's 'Request a magic link', or seed one directly for local testing).

request.description: The verified email ({{email}}) matches this registration's own primaryContact.contactEmail, so entitlement passes and a scoped access token is issued.

item.name: Verify for someone else's registration -> 403 REGISTRATION_ACCESS_DENIED

exec: pm.test('response does not leak the other business name', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include("Someone Else's Business"))

request.description: Proves that owning an inbox alone is not enough: the verified email ({{email}}) does not match otherReference's contact email, so this is refused even though the link itself is genuinely valid. Needs a FRESH, unused linkToken for this test (a magic link is single-use).

item.name: Verify with a non-existent reference -> same 403 (no disclosure)

exec: pm.test('code is REGISTRATION_ACCESS_DENIED (identical to a wrong-owner denial)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().code).to.eql('REGISTRATION_ACCESS_DENIED'))

request.description: Confirms the response is identical whether the reference doesn't exist or just isn't the caller's — the 403 never discloses which. Needs a FRESH, unused linkToken.

item.name: Verify with no reference -> unchanged base behaviour (no token)

request.description: Omitting reference entirely must behave exactly as the base magic-link design always has: verified, no entitlement check, no token, no lasting access. Needs a FRESH, unused linkToken.
Always GET immediately before a PATCH, to read the current version (optimistic concurrency).

item.name: PATCH own registration -> 200, updated + incremented version

exec: pm.test('businessName updated', () => pm.expect(body.businessName).to.eql('My Own Business Ltd (edited)'))

item.name: GET someone else's registration with a VALID token -> 403

exec: pm.test('no data leakage in the error body', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('businessName'); pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('otherReference')) })

request.description: A GENUINELY VALID token (correctly signed, not expired) for the WRONG reference. requireOwnRegistration rejects it before even reaching the repository, because the token's own claim doesn't name this reference.

item.name: PATCH someone else's registration with a VALID token -> 403
External-user token cannot reach an internal-only route (/search)

exec: pm.test('rejected (401/403/404), proving the two auth strategies are isolated', () => pm.expect([401, 403, 404]).to.include(pm.response.code))

request.description: /search requires the entra-bearer strategy (internal/staff). An external-user token, however validly signed for its own purpose, must be rejected here — the two strategies share nothing.

item.name: 5. Contact-email change revokes access
item.description: Run folder 2 and 3 first so externalAccessToken is set and valid.

item.name: Same (now-stale) token can no longer GET -> 403

exec: pm.test('status is 403 (grant revoked immediately, token itself unchanged)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403))

request.description: The token itself is still validly signed and not expired, but its persisted grant was revoked by the PATCH above (immediate, unconditional revocation on contact-email change — decision 6.4 in external-user-rbac-spec.html).
